Senses.Explanation: Literally “the one honored by the world,” this title names Śākyamuni as a figure invoked throughout the Chan record. The entry defines that figure through the record's public cases rather than an outside sacred biography. At the assembly on Vulture Peak, “the World-Honored One held up a flower; Kāśyapa smiled” (世尊拈花，迦葉微笑), and the account continues with entrusting “the treasury of the true teaching eye” to Mahākāśyapa. In the teaching-seat case, he mounts the seat; Mañjuśrī strikes the sounding block and says, “carefully observe the teaching king's teaching; the teaching king's teaching is thus” (諦觀法王法，法王法如是), whereupon the World-Honored One leaves the seat. Asked by an outsider not about words and not about no words, he remains silent for a while. The corpus also raises his birth gesture and declaration; Yunmen follows that recital with his own attributed statement that he would have struck him dead and fed him to a dog, “valuing peace throughout the world” (貴圖天下太平). Other cases have the World-Honored One direct Mañjuśrī and name Wangming Bodhisattva in the woman-in-composure exchange, point to the ground for a temple before Indra plants a blade of grass, and display a color-changing jewel while questioning the five heavenly kings. Later masters restage and compare these acts: Zhenjing Kewen raises his staff after reciting the flower case, and Zhanran Yuancheng compares the World-Honored One's mounting and silence with the same acts by the people before him. The Chan deviation is concrete and public: the title chiefly names the invoked figure who holds up the flower, mounts and leaves the teaching seat, pauses in an interview, and acts within repeatedly raised cases. Each later appraisal remains attributed to its speaker; none is made the World-Honored One's intention.
Senses.Note: The 8,093 exact matches occur in 406 allowlisted files. This is one title/person sense across the flower, teaching-seat, silence, birth, woman-in-composure, grass-temple, and jewel cases; different episodes do not create different referents. “Śākyamuni” (釋迦) is the name-form, and “old man Śākyamuni” (釋迦老子) is a separate familiar Chan form. Compare buddha (佛), Kāśyapa (迦葉), Ānanda (阿難), holding up the flower (拈花), mounting the seat (陞座), leaving the seat (下座), and remaining silent for a while (良久).

Occurrences.Kwic: 昔日靈山會上世尊拈花，迦葉微笑，世尊道：吾有正法眼藏分付摩訶大迦葉流傳，母令斷絕，至于今日。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Continued Essentials of the Old Worthies; a raised historical account: at the assembly on Vulture Peak the World-Honored One holds up a flower, Kāśyapa smiles, and the World-Honored One says that he entrusts the treasury of the true teaching eye to Mahākāśyapa for transmission.

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊陞座，文殊拍椎云：『諦觀法王法，法王法如是。』世尊便下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Chan Master Minshu; the complete raised case: the World-Honored One mounts the seat, Mañjuśrī strikes the block and announces, “Carefully observe the teaching king’s teaching; the teaching king’s teaching is thus,” and the World-Honored One immediately leaves the seat.

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊因外道問：不問有言，不問無言。世尊良久，外道歎曰：世尊大慈大悲，開我迷雲，令我得入。遂作禮而去。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Ancient Cases of the Chan School; the outsider asks neither about speech nor no speech, the World-Honored One remains silent for a while, and the outsider praises him and departs.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：世尊拈花，迦葉微笑。乃拈起拄杖曰：洞山拈起拄杖子，你諸人合作麼生？遂擊香卓。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Lamp Collection, Zhenjing Kewen section; after stating that the World-Honored One held up a flower and Kāśyapa smiled, Kewen raises his staff, asks what the assembly will do, and strikes the incense table.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且如世尊陞座，你諸人也陞座；世尊默然，你諸人也默然。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Record of Chan Master Zhanran Yuancheng; he says, “The World-Honored One mounted the seat; you people also mount the seat. The World-Honored One was silent; you people also are silent.” This anchors later direct redeployment of the two public acts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊初生時，一手指天，一手指地，周行七步，目顧四方，云：『天上天下，惟我獨尊。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Chan record raises the birth case: the World-Honored One points one hand to heaven and one to earth, walks seven steps, looks to the four directions, and says, “above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored” (天上天下，惟我獨尊).

Occurrences.Kwic: 不見世尊生下周行七步目顧四方。一手指天一手指地云。天上天下唯吾獨尊。雲門云。我當初若見一棒打殺與狗子喫却。何以如此。貴圖天下太平。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After reciting the World-Honored One's birth gesture and declaration, the record attributes to Yunmen: “if I had seen him at the time, I would have struck him dead with one blow and fed him to a dog,” followed by “valuing peace throughout the world” (貴圖天下太平). This preserves Yunmen's stated appraisal without assigning it to the World-Honored One.

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊命文殊出，文殊卻出女子定不得。世尊曰：『下方有罔明菩薩出得。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the woman-in-composure case, the World-Honored One commands Mañjuśrī to bring her out of composure. When Mañjuśrī cannot, he says, “below there is Wangming Bodhisattva, who can bring her out” (下方有罔明菩薩出得).

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊與眾行次，以手指地上云：『此處宜建梵剎。』天帝釋持一莖草插於地上云：『建梵剎已竟。』
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Walking with the assembly, the World-Honored One points to the ground and says, “a temple should be built here” (此處宜建梵剎). Indra plants a blade of grass and says, “the temple has already been built” (建梵剎已竟).

Occurrences.Kwic: 世尊一日示隨色摩尼珠。問五方天王。此珠而作何色。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The World-Honored One displays a color-changing jewel to the five heavenly kings and asks, “what color does this jewel make?” (此珠而作何色). This anchors another display-and-question case.
